title: Hot take: Saving Private Ryan was not nearly as sad as everyone says it is

commenti.body:
I didn't know that sad was a common description for it! Sobering and heavy maybe, but never heard sad! 

I have always viewed it as just a big epic film with particular attention paid to grounding it in realism(at least in the beginning). Any feelings of sadness got lost in the scale and spectacle of it all whenever I watched. 

Overall, I guess I agree, I can't really pinpoint a specific emotion for it. I think the movie as a whole is just kind of one big "Significant Emotional Event"

This is annoying. The movie is about a bunch of people dying to save one man because all of his brothers have already died during an atrocious war where pretty much every other sense of humanity was lost a long time ago. It is inherently sad. Whether you cried or not isn't a hot take. It's a combination of people building it up and deciding to watch movies in some sort of *cry race*. Watch it again and try to connect with the subject matter instead of playing "try not to cry".
do you feel sad when you read a history textbook about war?

Yes! I completely agree with this. But the response to me not feeling sadness is the tired old "you're just trying not to cry" thing. It's not like I'm averse to crying in a movie for some reason. It's just that SPR doesn't hit that particular emotional chord for me

You’re 100% right. 

It’s not a “try not to cry” challenge. OP posted his fucking substack page like fuck off. He’s not even a good writer

It certainly dances with sadness, but I kind of feel like it's meant to purposely create an absurd feeling in you within you tied to it. 

Now that the old gears are turning in my head, it's interesting that I never registered explicit sadness, but i think that's the actual intention. It opens with an absolute meat grinder of impersonal slaughter. 24 minutes of mayhem, crying, suffering. The dead are all nameless. Most are basically children, one literally was calling out for his mom. It's so horrifying that it is beyond sad.

Then it focuses way in, and we are given the main characters who undertake a heroic mission together and sacrifice everything. It's sad when each one dies, but it was kind of hard to feel in the grand scheme of the movie because they all get to die with dignity and heroically. 

*After typing this, my dad informed me that when we first saw the movie I DID have tears in my eyes when Giovanni Ribisi died.

The question supposes that you’re meant to hold a narrative film at the same emotional level as a history textbook. It’s so skewed I’m surprised you only have 12 downvotes. 

But yeah, I do. Atrocities make me sad. Call me a pussy.
